title: The Noticeboard
story:
Taped to the side of the rack, in Kip's round handwriting:

"The noticeboard lived on port 8081 of the old server and now it is just gone?? Everybody's bookmarks point at :8081. Sauna rota, ferry dates, who stole the last of the good coffee. It's the Apache one (`httpd:2.4-alpine`). Please bring it back!! - Kip"

Below it, in Ingrid's neat hand: "Same port as before. The container is called `noticeboard`."
objectives: Run `httpd:2.4-alpine` detached as a container named `noticeboard`
Publish it so that `http://localhost:8081` reaches the web server (container port 80)
startingState: No containers exist. The `httpd:2.4-alpine` image is already downloaded.
hints: A container has its own private network. To reach a service inside it from the outside, you publish one of its ports on the host.
The publish flag is `-p HOST_PORT:CONTAINER_PORT`. The Apache image listens on port 80 inside the container, and the crew expects 8081 on the outside.

```bash
docker run -d --name noticeboard -p 8081:80 httpd:2.4-alpine
curl http://localhost:8081
```
debrief: `-p 8081:80` maps host port 8081 to container port 80, so the left number is what clients use and the right one is what the app listens on. Pro tip: `docker port noticeboard` prints the active mappings.
